newsitem.title: IRAQ: Russian traders, politicians hold talks in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Russian traders, politicians hold talks in Iraq.

text.p: Several Russian businessmen and politicians are holding talks with Iraqi officials on improving relations and business links under an oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, Iraqi newspapers said on Thursday.

They said the Russians led by Sergei Baborin, deputy speaker of parliament, were given a red-carpet welcome by Iraqi officials, including Vice-President Taha Yassin Ramadan, Deputy Premier Tareq Aziz and Foreign Minister Mohammad Saeed al-Sahaf.
"Aziz stressed (to the Russians) Iraq's desire to continue and improve its ties with Russia," al-Iraq daily said.
Ten days ago, the Iraqi National Assembly ratified an oil contract with Russia under which Moscow is expected to develop seven to eight billion barrels of reserves in Iraq's southern Qurna oilfield.
Oil investment violates U.N. sanctions imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. But Russian officials said the contract would not start before the end of the curbs.

Moscow is also seeking to sell to Baghdad foodstuffs in return for buying oil under the oil-for-food deal with the United Nations which went into effect in December. The deal allows Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil over six months to buy urgently needed items.
"Sergei Baborin...stresses that his country will exert efforts in order to end the economic embargo on Iraq during this year," the paper said.
